content: The dataset includes information on food consumption patterns among infants and young children (IYC) across various countries and regions. The data is categorized by geographic scope, nature of the sample, age groups, and specific uses such as food item lists (FL), percentage of IYC consuming food items (PERC), and quantities consumed (QTY). Below is a detailed breakdown of the data: 1. Ecuador (2012): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=0) and 12-23 months (n=471). The data was used for FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 2. Mexico (2012): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=222) and 12-23 months (n=518). The data contributed to FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 3. Peru (2015): Sub-national data was collected from highland regions (Huancavelica Region) for children aged 6-11 months (n=79) and 12-23 months (n=118). The data was used for FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 4. United States (2011-2012): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=170) and 12-23 months (n=206). The data contributed to FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 5. Bangladesh (2011-2012): Nationally representative data (rural only) was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=190) and 12-23 months (n=443). The data was used for FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 6. India (2009-2012): Nationally representative data (rural only) was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=25) and 12-23 months (n=827). The data contributed to FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 7. Israel (2009-2012): Nationally representative cohort data was collected for children aged 12-15 months (n=887). The data was used for PERC analyses only. 8. Korea (2017): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=3) and 12-23 months (n=66). The data was used for FL analyses only. 9. Bulgaria (2007): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=432) and 12-23 months (n=282). The data contributed to FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 10. Germany (2008): Sub-national urban data was collected from Dortmund and surrounding areas for children aged 12-23 months (n=173). The data was used for FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 11. Portugal (2015-2016): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=209) and 12-23 months (n=409). The data contributed to FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 12. United Kingdom (2011): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=1292) and 12-17 months (n=1275). The data was used for FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 13. Ethiopia (2011): Sub-national data covering Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, and SNNP regions was collected for children aged 6-8 months (n=497), 9-11 months (n=464), and 12-23 months (n=1537). The data was used for FL and QTY analyses. 14. Ghana (2014): Sub-national data from Karaga and Gomoa East districts was collected for children aged 6-8 months (n=190), 9-11 months (n=195), and 12-23 months (n=321). The data contributed to FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 15. Kenya (2017-2018): Sub-national data from Elgeyo Marakwet County was collected for children aged 6-23 months. The data was used for FL analyses only. 16. Senegal (2013-2015): Urban/peri-urban clinic-based data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=72) and 12-23 months (n=146). The data was used for PERC analyses only. 17. South Africa (2007): Sub-national rural data from KwaZulu Natal was collected for children aged 6-12 months (n=475). The data contributed to FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 18. Tanzania (2013-2015): Urban/peri-urban clinic-based data from Dar es Salaam was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=79) and 12-23 months (n=150). The data was used for PERC analyses only. 19. Brazil (2019): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-11 months (n=1414) and 12-23 months (n=2938). The data contributed to FL and PERC analyses. 20. Colombia (2010-2011): Sub-national hospital-based data from Bogotá was collected for children aged ~12 months (n=72). The data was used for FL analyses only. 21. Guatemala (2015-2016): Sub-national data from prioritized areas based on stunting was collected for children aged 6-8 months (n=453), 9-11 months (n=280), and 12-23 months (n=1127). The data contributed to FL, PERC, and QTY analyses. 22. Singapore (2010-2011): Sub-national hospital-based data was collected for children aged 6 months (n=760), 9 months (n=893), and 12 months (n=907). The data was used for FL analyses only. 23. Thailand (2003-2005): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-8 months (n=60), 9-11 months (n=51), and 12-23 months (n=202). The data contributed to FL and QTY analyses. 24. Vietnam (2009): Nationally representative data was collected for children aged 6-8 months, 9-11 months, and 12-23 months (sample size not available). The data was used for FL and QTY analyses. 25. Australia (2009-2010): Sub-national data from Brisbane and South Australia was collected for children aged 14 months (n=409) and 24 months (n=363). The data contributed to FL and QTY analyses. 26. New Zealand (1998-1999): Sub-national data from three cities was collected for children aged 6-35 months. The data was used for FL analyses only. 27. Europe Multi-Country Study (2002-2010): Data from study centers in Germany, Belgium, Italy, Poland, and Spain was collected for children aged ~12 months (n=633). The data was used for FL analyses only. 28. Czech Republic (1999-2000): Sub-national data from Prague was collected for children aged 9 months (n=97), 12 months (n=87), and 24 months (n=88). The data contributed to FL and PERC analyses. 29. France (2005-2009): Sub-national data from Dijon and surrounding cities was collected for children aged 0-12 months (n=268). The data was used for FL analyses only. This dataset provides a comprehensive overview of food consumption patterns among infants and young children across diverse geographic and socio-economic contexts. It highlights the variability in data collection methods, sample sizes, and the specific uses of the data for dietary analyses.
